Life expectancy at birth, years, 2023 to 2025

key_takeaways: Current health expenditure was 10.0 percent of GDP in 2024, above the OECD mean of 9.3 percent.{{health_system.financing:1}}
Elective treatment within four months reached 72.6 percent in April to June 2026, against a 95 percent goal.{{health_system.public_system:6}}
Health New Zealand's deficit narrowed from NZ$835 million to NZ$369 million in 2025/26 on the Treasury basis.{{health_system.outlook:10}}
International graduates are 43.5 percent of the doctor register, yet only 40 percent stay two years.{{health_system.workforce:1}}
health_system: Tax-funded universal coverage serves permanent residents, and the Accident Compensation Corporation pays for injury care without fault.{{health_system.public_system:1}}
Patients enroll with a general practice, and 36 percent of practices were closed to new enrolments in 2024.{{health_system.public_system:12}}{{health_system.public_system:9}}
Nurse density is 12.4 per 1,000 people, above the OECD mean of 9.9.{{health_system.workforce:3}}
market: Private insurance covers 35 percent of adults, and Southern Cross holds about 60 percent of the insurance market.{{health_system.private_system:1}}{{health_system.private_system:2}}
The OECD counts 171 hospitals, 92 public and 79 private.{{health_system.hospitals:1}}
Health New Zealand signed its first long-term private hospital contracts in 2026, worth about NZ$300 million.{{health_system.private_system:7}}
risks: The election outcome stays open until the 27 November final count and will shape budget priorities.{{health_system.outlook:7}}
Partners Life raised premiums on existing policies by 18, 20 and 23 percent in 2025.{{health_system.private_system:1}}
By 2030/31 superannuation and finance costs will take about 28 percent of the tax take.{{country_overview.economy:4}}

recent.text: Budget 2026 added more than NZ$5.8 billion (US$3.29 billion) in new health operating funding over the forecast period.{{recent_developments.4:1}}
The 7 November election left National, ACT and New Zealand First with 67 seats, under a caretaker government.{{recent_developments.2:1}}{{recent_developments.2:2}}
The 2025/26 Health Survey found 5.9 percent of adults smoking daily, the first reading below 6 percent.{{recent_developments.0:1}}

country_background: New Zealand, a constitutional monarchy with its capital in Wellington, had about 5.37 million residents at 30 September 2026.{{country_overview.demographics:7}}{{country_overview.demographics:15}}{{country_overview.demographics:1}} The 7 November 2026 general election has not produced a government. Provisional results give National, ACT and New Zealand First 67 seats, a narrow majority that special votes in the 27 November final count could remove, and Prime Minister Christopher Luxon leads a caretaker government.{{country_overview.government:3}}{{country_overview.government:4}}{{country_overview.government:5}} GDP was about 305 billion international dollars (purchasing power parity) in 2025, but unemployment reached 5.7 percent in the September 2026 quarter.{{country_overview.economy:1}}{{country_overview.economy:5}} Life expectancy is 80.4 years for men and 83.7 for women, and about 17 percent of residents are 65 or older.{{country_overview.demographics:5}}{{country_overview.demographics:4}} The key risk is fiscal: the Treasury warns that unchecked demographics make the fiscal position unsustainable.{{country_overview.economy:4}}
